Is Now a Good Time to Buy Stocks?
article:
“Should I buy stocks now or wait for the market to fall further?”
This is a question many investors find themselves asking after periods of market volatility.
Buying too early and watching prices continue to fall can make some uneasy.
But waiting too long might mean missing a market recovery.
Why Investors Are Hesitating to Buy Stocks
The
Straits Times Index
(SGX: ^STI) had a great start this year.
It climbed steadily and reached a record of 5,801.96 on 4 September 2026.
Lately, however, it has been pulling back.
The STI has since fallen 8.6% from its record high, dropping to 5,303.82 on 2 November 2026.
Investors are becoming more cautious as uncertainty surrounding interest rates, economic growth and
geopolitical tensions
influences global markets.
Negative headlines can weaken investor confidence, and investors worry about buying just before a downturn.
When prices fall immediately following a purchase, investors may regret it, which prompts them to wait until market conditions appear more stable before buying again.
Waiting for that “perfect” price is challenging because markets are unpredictable.
Hesitating too long may lead to missed opportunities.
Three Reasons to Consider Buying Stocks Now
1. Market declines can create attractive valuations
Falling share prices can present opportunities to buy quality companies at more reasonable valuations.
The share price of
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05) fell by approximately 16% in early April 2025.
This occurred despite DBS reporting a record net profit of S$11.4 billion for FY2024, an 11% year-on-year increase.
Investors should note that the market sell-off was primarily driven by macroeconomic conditions, including US tariff announcements, as well as a scheduled ex-dividend date on 7 April, rather than issues with the underlying business.
Look beyond share prices and analyse the company’s price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, cash flow and long-term growth prospects.
2. Time in the market matters more than timing the market
Staying invested
allows investors to enjoy growth and better returns as a result of compounding.
Investors who bought DBS shares just before the dip in April 2025 and held them until 30 October 2026 would have seen a nearly 60% capital gain.
Shares purchased on 1 April 2025 at S$45.62 each were worth S$73.13 on 30 October 2026.
3. Dividend investors can benefit from lower entry prices
If a company continues paying the same annual dividend while its share price declines, investors purchasing at the lower price receive a higher yield relative to their investment.
However, investors should prioritise dividend sustainability by assessing a company’s earnings, cash flow and payout ratio rather than being attracted solely to a high headline yield.
Three Reasons Why Waiting Might Make Sense
1. Stock valuations may still be expensive
A market decline does not automatically mean that stocks are cheap.
Investors should assess valuations using the P/E ratio and the price-to-book (P/B) ratio.
They should also consider future earnings expectations, as overly optimistic forecasts may already be reflected in share prices.
2. Corporate earnings could deteriorate
Slower economic growth, weaker consumer demand and rising operating costs can reduce profitability.
Find out whether the falling share prices reflect temporary market weakness or deeper structural problems.
3. Your financial circumstances may not support investing yet
Rather than asking “should I invest now?”, ask whether you can afford to.
Money required within the next few years for essential commitments is unsuitable for stock market investments since markets can experience significant fluctuations and may not recover in time when funds are needed.
Having a stable financial foundation helps investors avoid being forced to sell shares at unfavourable prices.
Buy Now or Wait: What Does History Tell Us?
Stock markets can recover surprisingly quickly after sharp declines.
The S&P 500 plunged approximately 34% from its February 2020 peak of 3,386.15 during the COVID-19 sell-off in March 2020.
However, on 18 August 2020, despite the ongoing pandemic, the index pushed past the February record to close at 3,389.78.
Investors who waited for complete certainty before returning to the market risked missing a significant portion of the rebound.
Still, neither buying now nor waiting guarantees better results, as the outcome depends on market movements and investment timing.
A Smarter Approach: Invest Gradually Instead of Guessing the Bottom
Dollar-cost averaging (DCA) involves investing a fixed amount at regular intervals, regardless of market movements.
The same investment amount buys more shares when share prices decrease.
This approach reduces the need to find an ideal time to buy, although it does not ensure profits.
Maintaining a cash reserve enables you to take advantage of opportunities during market declines.
Investors who have cash reserves can purchase shares when high-quality companies experience temporary price drops.
However, holding excessive cash indefinitely while waiting for the perfect buying opportunity can result in missed market gains.
Rather than attempting to predict short-term price movements, investors should prioritise quality companies with strong balance sheets.
Businesses with manageable debt, established competitive advantages and reliable earnings are better positioned to navigate economic uncertainty and downturns.
That said, even a financially strong company can be a poor investment if purchased at an excessive valuation.
What Should Singapore Investors Do Today?
Long-term investors may benefit from starting or continuing to invest during periods of market uncertainty.
Exchange-traded funds (ETFs)
reduce reliance on individual stocks, providing exposure to a broad range of holdings.
Investors could consider adding established Singapore blue chips, such as DBS and
Singapore Telecommunications Limited
(SGX: Z74), better known as Singtel, as part of a diversified portfolio.
Income investors must assess whether companies can sustain their payouts over the long term.
Important indicators include payout ratios, operating cash flow, earnings consistency and debt levels.
A market correction may create opportunities to accumulate shares in established dividend-paying companies at lower prices.
Be cautious of unusually high yields, as these may reflect falling share prices or business health concerns.
Beginners or those uncomfortable with volatility may prefer a gradual investment approach with DCA.
DCA helps reduce the emotional pressure associated with market timing while allowing beginners to gain experience and confidence over time.
Diversification across different sectors and geographical markets is also important to reduce individual company risks.
Get Smart: Don’t Wait for the Perfect Moment
Rather than asking “is now a good time to buy stocks?”, ask whether your financial circumstances, investment objectives and the current market valuations support investing now.
Market declines can create opportunities, but not every falling stock is good value.
Investing gradually in quality businesses with DCA may be more practical than trying to predict the next market movement.

title: iX Biopharma says Orion Speciality Labs’ lack of state licence is ‘expected’ at current stage
article:
The board of directors for iX Biopharma confirms that Orion Speciality Lab (Orion) has not yet obtained the licence from the Nevada State Board of Pharmacy.

In the Nov 3 response to SGX’s queries, the company mentioned that this is expected at the current stage, as the licence follows a set of sequence.

“The joint venture between Orion and iX Biopharma first needs to be in place before presenting to the Nevada State Board of Pharamancy. Also, production equipment needs to be installed and be ready for inspection,” the company clarifies.

iX Biopharma mentioned that once these are in place, both parties can submit a manufacturing plan with supporting documents to the Board for review, followed by an inspection of the facility.

“The timing of the Nevada licence is therefore in line with our plans,” the company confirms.

With regards to the Oct 20 article from Politico stating that Orion’s licence application has been tabled on two occasions, iX Biopharma clarifies that any prior application was made by Orion itself.

See also: Sats contractors under MOM probe for false occupation and salary declaration of foreign workers

iX Biopharma adds that the contract with the US Department of Defense (DoD) for the development of Wafermine, awarded in February, is not tied to Orion's site.

“For Wafermine’s supply under the EUA, we are evaluating a number of manufacturing pathways, of which Orion’s site is an option,” the company says.

Meanwhile, iX Biopharma explained its Nov 10, 2025 announcement mentioning that Orion had “operationally ready infrastructure and regulatory licences” means that with Orion being a registered 503B outsourcing facility, meant that the company will not need to build its own US facility from the ground up.

See also: LBD Engineering GM charged with operating dormitory without licence, to step down as subsidiary Metrocon's chairman

“Operationally ready infrastructure referred to Orion's site having the infrastructure ready to host our manufacturing while Regulatory licences referred to Orion's registration with the FDA as a 503B outsourcing facility, which Orion held at the time of the announcement and still holds,” the company states.

Finally, iX Biopharma confirms that there has been no change in joint venture negotiations since the AGM on Oct 16 and both parties are at an advanced stage of negotiations on the final terms and have been carrying out due diligence and tax assessments.

Shares of iX Biopharma closed 3 cents lower, or down 5.88% at 48 cents on Nov 3.

title: Pfizer raises 2026 forecast, extending pharma windfall
article:
(Nov 3): Pfizer Inc raised its full-year outlook after it outperformed in the third quarter, as growing demand for its newer medicines helped the drugmaker offset declining sales of its Covid-19 products.

The drugmaker now expects full-year revenue of US$62 billion to US$64 billion and adjusted earnings of US$2.95 to US$3.05 a share. It previously forecast revenue of US$60.5 billion to US$62.5 billion and adjusted earnings of US$2.80 to US$3 a share.

The New York-based drugmaker reported better-than-anticipated third-quarter profit and sales. It’s the latest pharma company to surpass Wall Street expectations during the period. Last week, Eli Lilly & Co, Merck & Co and Bristol Myers Squibb Co were all among companies that raised their annual forecast.

Shares rose less than 1% in early trading in New York on Tuesday. They’ve gained 23% so far this year, through Monday’s close.

Pfizer is trying to reinvent itself after a major pandemic windfall. CEO Albert Bourla has turned to acquisitions, new cancer medicines and an ambitious push into obesity treatments to revive growth as Covid-19 sales fade and some of the company’s biggest drugs face competition from cheaper alternatives.

One of Pfizer’s major bets is in obesity, where it is seeking to challenge market leaders Eli Lilly & Co and Novo Nordisk A/S. Pfizer bought Metsera Inc last year, gaining experimental treatments including a shot designed to be taken once a month rather than weekly. The company is now advancing an extensive clinical programme to test whether its medicines can compete in the rapidly expanding market.

See also: Neuralink’s China rival targets obesity with ‘electronic’ GLP-1

Cancer is another major focus. Pfizer’s US$43 billion acquisition of Seagen gave it a portfolio of cancer medicines, including Padcev, a treatment for bladder cancer. Sales of that drug beat estimates in the third quarter.

Sales of heart drug Vyndaqel were US$1.77 billion, slightly higher than estimates. Revenues from pneumococcal vaccine Prevnar were US$1.56 billion while the blood thinner Eliquis brought in US$2.52 billion in the quarter.

Pfizer is also seeking to improve profitability through aggressive cost cutting. Separately, the company said Tuesday interim chief financial officer Cecile Guegan would take on the role permanently.

title: Audi and Mercedes hit by walkouts in union push for higher wages
article:
(Nov 3): German metalworkers are stepping up nationwide stoppages as labour officials pursue wage increases and stronger job protections, escalating a dispute affecting about 3.7 million employees.

Companies including Volkswagen AG’s Audi unit, Mercedes-Benz Group AG and Schaeffler AG were hit by walkouts on Monday and Tuesday after a mandatory truce period expired at the end of October.

Germany’s IG Metall union is demanding a 5% wage increase over 12 months and measures to protect jobs and production sites. As part of the latest round of negotiations, employers have offered a one-time payment in 2027 equivalent to 1% of annual gross pay and a 1.3% wage increase effective in July 2028.

The talks come at a particularly challenging time for Germany’s car industry. Automakers are seeking to cut costs as they contend with weak demand in China and heightened domestic competition. Suppliers are also suffering, with Schaeffler AG announcing Tuesday it plans to close five sites in Europe and eliminate 3,460 jobs, some three-quarters of those in Germany.

More significant staffing reductions will be unavoidable, employer representatives warned during the latest negotiating round, unless Germany can substantially reduce hourly labour costs. A third round of talks is due to begin on Thursday, according to IG Metall.

Tensions are especially acute at Ingolstadt-based Audi, where workers grappling with the rising cost of living, particularly prices for energy and fuel, joined a brief stoppage last night.

See also: Tesla Cybercab cruises into Singapore

CEO Gernot Döllner has faced criticism after appearing last month at a campaign event with US President Donald Trump. While Döllner announced plans for Audi’s first US factory at the rally, unions have called for long-term guarantees for German sites.

title: CSE Global secures $434.9 mil new orders in 3QFY2026, up nearly 200% y-o-y
article:
CSE Global has secured $434.9 million in new orders for 3QFY2026 ended Sept 30, up 197.7% y-o-y.

During the quarter, CSE Global’s electrification business segment saw a surge of 937% y-o-y in new order intake to $320.3 million, driven by the two contracts secured in the United States (US) worth $254.8 million for the design and manufacture of power distribution centres and the integration of complex electrical and control systems and equipment for the Cheyenne Power Hub project and the Liquified Natural Gas market.

Meanwhile, the communications business segment saw a 15.8% y-o-y in order intake to $63.3 million in 3QFY2026.

The Automation business segment saw a 28.1% y-o-y growth in order intake to $51.3 million in new orders, representing 11.8% of total order intake for the quarter.

With these new orders, CSE Global’s order book stood at $728.5 million for 3QFY2026.

Shares of CSE Global closed 0.5 cents higher, or up 0.55% at 91.5 cents on Nov 3.

title: US seeks deeper Myanmar ties, access to ‘bountiful’ rare earths
article:
(Nov 3): The US plans to deepen engagement with Myanmar’s military-backed government to counter China’s influence and gain access to the war-torn nation’s vast rare-earth deposits.

According to a State Department strategy document published last month, the US aims to become a “major trading partner and supplier” in Myanmar and see the Southeast Asian nation triple imports of American goods and agriculture products by 2030.

It also plans to take an active role in nationwide peace discussions over the same period “to increase US influence and create an environment for US investment over other regional actors”.

Washington and its Western allies heavily sanctioned the regime following its 2021 coup. That isolation allowed Beijing to cement a strategic foothold by funding infrastructure projects and dominating critical mineral supply chains, often leveraging relationships with factions controlling resource-rich territories.

Myanmar is among the most commodity-rich nations on the planet, with significant resources including natural gas, copper, coal, teak, gemstones, tin, gold and rare earths, of which the country is the world’s fourth-largest supplier.

Since being installed as president in April, former coup leader Min Aung Hlaing has launched a diplomatic campaign to bring Myanmar back into the international fold, making high-profile state visits to China, India and Malaysia.

The US strategy also aims to advance “fiscal federalism and territorial demarcation” that will create opportunities to access the country’s “bountiful rare earth resources and combat scam centres", the document states. It adds that expanding diplomatic efforts “will advance Administration priorities to counter China’s influence and promote a free and open Indo-Pacific”.

title: Eurogroup calls for ECB presidency nominations by Nov 6
article:
(Nov 3): Euro-area governments have been asked to submit nominations for successors to European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde by Friday.

Eurogroup President Kyriakos Pierrakakis has called on member states to send proposals by Nov 6, according to a spokesperson of the group that comprises finance ministers from the 21-nation euro zone. Ministers will take stock of the nominations at a meeting on Nov 9.

So far, candidates include Pablo Hernandez de Cos, a former governor of Spain’s central bank who currently leads the Bank for International Settlements, and former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot.

Lagarde said Thursday that she will step down on Feb 7, about nine months early, to be able to speak out on topics beyond monetary policy. In the past, she has expressed an interest in contributing to discussions around next year’s French presidential election.

Finding a successor is part of a larger reshuffle encompassing three of the ECB Executive Board’s six seats. Isabel Schnabel, who oversees markets, and Chief Economist Philip Lane are both nearing the end of their tenures and the process to replace them has also begun.

See also: US moves to revoke South Africa, Rwanda duty-free trade access

For Schnabel, who is set to leave in early January, about a year before her eight-year term finishes, the Eurogroup extended a deadline for applications to Nov 27. Lane’s mandate expires in May.

European leaders will convene on Nov 26-27 in Brussels and are expected to make progress on the appointments, including Lagarde’s replacement. They will meet for an informal session two weeks before that.

De Cos and Knot have been travelling around the region in recent months to convince governments they are the right person for the job. In the end, though, it will likely come down to support from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who has met with both of them, and French President Emmanuel Macron.

title: IPO review functions under MAS to be consolidated under SGX RegCo from Jan 4, 2027
article:
The Singapore Exchange Regulation (SGX RegCo) will be taking over the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) prospectus review functions for both Mainboard and Global Listing Board (GLB) listing applications from Jan 4, 2027.

“This change allows us to streamline the IPO process and give issuers greater regulatory certainty,” says SGX RegCo CEO Tan Boon Gin in a statement on Nov 3. The consolidation was first mooted by the Equities Market Review Group and the MAS conducted a public consultation on the proposal from Oct 29, 2025 to Nov 29, 2025.

Previously, a prospective issuer had to file its prospectus and listing application to MAS and SGX RegCo respectively for review. From Jan 4 onwards, issuers will only have to submit their prospectuses and listing applications to SGX RegCo via their electronic submissions portal.

SGX RegCo says it expects to process all complete listing applications within six to eight weeks under the new arrangement. MAS will continue to oversee SGX RegCo’s regulatory responsibilities and retains the power to determine and grant exemptions from prospectus disclosure requirements under the Securities and Futures Act.

Aside from consolidating MAS’s IPO review functions, SGX RegCo says it will be standing down the Listings Advisory Committee (LAC) to further reduce regulatory touchpoints. The LAC was created before SGX RegCo and was originally established to address concerns about SGX’s independence in the listing policymaking and review process.

Law firms and issuer managers who participated in MAS’s public consultation last year expressed their support for the changes. SGX RegCo says it will continue to solicit feedback from market participants as these changes are implemented and will roll out further enhancements when needed.

See also: Turnover for 11 stocks with reduced board lot sizes traded 3.6% higher than broader STI stocks: SGX CEO

“Singapore investors have become more sophisticated, and they have access to more information of higher quality,” Tan says. “Equity investing has also become much more global in nature. This requires an evolution of our philosophies and roles.”

“Moving to a disclosure-based approach allows market forces to take the place of merit-based judgements by regulators. SGX RegCo’s role in such a disclosure-based regime will be focused on ensuring proper disclosures so that investment decision-making takes place in the market – where such decisions rightfully reside.”

title: Malaysia's IOI Properties to launch Singapore private fund in next few months, secondary listing in early 2027
article:
PUTRAJAYA (Nov 3): IOI Properties Group Bhd is looking to launch a private real estate fund for its Singapore assets in the next few months.

The property developer has started marketing the fund backed by assets worth $6 billion to investors, chief executive officer Datuk Lee Yeow Seng said on Tuesday. A sale of a 50% stake in the fund, illustratively, could raise nearly RM10 billion ($3.14 billion) for IOI Properties, he said.

“That would be quite significant,” Lee said at a briefing after unveiling the prospectus for IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust's initial public offering....(click here for the full story on theedgemalaysia.com).

title: China plans broad AI guardrails after global security lapses
article:
(Nov 3): China plans to roll out a broad set of standards governing the artificial intelligence (AI) safety from development through deployment, representing some of the most comprehensive guidelines to guard against a loss of control over increasingly powerful AI.

The country’s state economic planner on Tuesday said it’s quickening legislation to govern and oversee how AI is developed and applied, covering the entire life cycle of models. The regulations will extend to areas from data to computing power, said Wang Ruomeng, a senior official with the National Development and Reform Commission. That encompasses developers from DeepSeek to Moonshot and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, which are leading a nationwide effort to create models that can hold their own against the best from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Wang’s comments reflect Beijing’s attempt to strike a delicate balance in countering the US in a key arena, while recognising the potential for AI to run amok or fuel cyberattacks. Global concerns have grown since warnings from Silicon Valley leaders that the technology poses existential risks to humanity, and a spate of recent hacks in which AI went rogue or radically enhanced cyberbreach attempts.

“We will accelerate legislation to support core AI enablers — data, computing power and algorithms — and regulate key application scenarios, while establishing safety standards and ethical guidelines covering the full life cycle of AI,” Wang said at a briefing in Beijing on Tuesday. The authorities will carry out regular reviews of how the rules are implemented and revise provisions that become outdated, he said.

China and the US agreed in September to try and develop a common understanding of the technology’s benefits and threats. That preceded a summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington, where AI was a key topic.

Beijing intends to ease the burden of compliance on AI firms via an unspecified transition period and guidance. It plans to roll out sector-specific regulatory sandboxes to allow greater leeway for trial and error, Wang added.

See also: Chinese stock sell-off resumes as rescue tools face scepticism

At the same time, industry developers and operators should bolster risk management and disclose safety risks, incidents and vulnerabilities, he said.

The Chinese government will also monitor AI’s impact on employment and displacement, Wang said, underscoring Beijing’s opposition to the large-scale social dislocations that may arise as AI gets more useful. It will provide broad safety-net protections for workers affected, he said.

Still, China intends to adhere closely to the playbook that triggered the widespread adoption of home-grown AI models across the globe. The government continues to encourage open AI development during the 15th five-year plan ending 2030, he said. Wang also called on countries to deepen mutual trust and cooperate on safety governance, coordinate vulnerability disclosures and risk responses, and build confidence in each other’s AI systems.

“AI safety is not a problem one company, industry or country can tackle alone — it is a global challenge requiring international cooperation,” Wang said.

title: Neuralink’s China rival targets obesity with ‘electronic’ GLP-1
article:
(Nov 3): Chinese neurotechnology firm BrainCo is developing a wearable device that it says could suppress appetite by stimulating the brain, positioning it as a potential non-drug alternative to blockbuster GLP-1 weight-loss treatments.

The company aims to bring the device to market within the next two to three years, according to founding partner Nyx He, who spoke in an interview at the Bloomberg Tech London event.

The product would effectively function as an “electronic version of GLP-1” obesity drugs, He said. The company plans to launch the device first in China before potentially expanding to the US.

BrainCo — which seeks to compete with Elon Musk’s Neuralink — is aiming to apply its brain-computer interface, or BCI, technology for the weight-loss market. The sector is currently dominated by GLP-1 drugs Wegovy and Zepbound, which mimic metabolic hormones that regulate appetite. The Hangzhou-based firm’s effort would represent an expansion beyond its existing business in neurotherapy devices, prosthetics and robotics.

She declined to comment on BrainCo’s plans to go public or raise additional funds before a listing. The company has filed confidentially for a Hong Kong initial public offer, Bloomberg News reported in January.

The company will explore different ways to commercialise the product, including potentially releasing separate medical and consumer versions, according to He.

See also: Bayer raises profit outlook on strong demand for drugs

It currently markets BCI-enabled headsets to address neurological disorders such as autism, ADHD and insomnia. The devices collect, decode and in some cases stimulate neural signals.

Beyond wearables, BrainCo develops prosthetic hands that allow amputees and people with disabilities to control lifelike fingers using brain signals, enabling tasks such as playing the piano and practising calligraphy. In recent years, it’s supplied robotic hands to China’s fast-expanding humanoid robotics industry.

Despite growing geopolitical scrutiny around BCI technology, including proposed US curbs on investment in Chinese BCI firms, He said BrainCo continues to see “great market acceptance” for its prosthetic hand in the US and expects the growth to accelerate.

See also: Danone sales rise on higher prices, medical nutrition demand

“We still see huge demand for our products, both the robotic hands for humanoid and prosthetic hands for amputees,” she said.

Although BrainCo has historically focused on non-invasive BCI, the company may expand into invasive approaches that require brain implants in the future, He said.
